title: Triage Flow: SLO Heatmap + Contextual Playbook Snippets for Rapid Handoffs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact triage surface inside the Redwood Console that surfaces an SLO heatmap alongside contextual playbook snippets and one-click postmortem links. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-action during incidents by making SLO impact, recommended steps, and historical postmortem artifacts visible in a single, keyboard-accessible panel. Primary users: on-call engineers and incident commanders. Constraints: must fit the existing console layout, respect RBAC (show/hide playbook content for restricted roles), and avoid introducing noise for low-priority alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows SLO heatmap with per-route shading and hover details for error budget burn and expected time-to-breach
Contextual playbook snippets (2–3 actionable steps) surface inline with a link to full runbook and latest postmortem
Keyboard shortcut opens compact triage panel and focuses first suggested action
Design provides compact + expanded modes for mobile and wide screens
Design includes microcopy for role-based visibility and data freshness (last updated timestamp)
comments: 2026-03-05 - Asha: Kickoff — interviewed two on-call engineers and a reliability PM. Key insight: engineers want immediate answer to 'what do I do next' and a single place to copy a runbook step into a Slack incident channel.
2026-03-06 - Luca: Wireframes created for compact triage strip and expanded drawer. Iteration focuses on heatmap micro-legend and sticky action bar.
2026-03-08 - PM review (Riley Chen): Prefer SLO delta timeline clipped to last 15m by default. Suggest adding 'confidence' markers when data is sampled or estimated.
2026-03-09 - Security review note (Nina Kapoor): Playbook snippets must not expose sensitive runbook entries; add role gating and a 'redacted' state in the mockups.
2026-03-10 - Design critique: reduce color saturation for heatmap to avoid alarm fatigue; introduce pattern overlays for monotonic degradation vs noisy spikes.

2026-03-11 - Engineering sync (Jamal Ortiz): Backend can provide summarized playbook snippets via the runbook API and a 'postmortem_shortlink' field; agreed to add a 'cached_at' timestamp for freshness.

2026-03-12 - Prototype uploaded to Figma and linked below. Next: usability test with 4 on-call engineers and one SRE lead, then handoff to FE for a lightweight A/B (compact vs. no-compact) during the next oncall rotation.
Follow-ups: create ENG ticket for accessibility review, ENG ticket for RBAC checks, PM to scope analytics events (triage_opened, action_clicked, postmortem_viewed).
